tone_statements.quote: We will give a preliminary illustration of this by studying the loans made by Cemuhi, a tonal language from the centre of the mainland, from the non-tonal languages that surround it to the north (see Map 1). [...] These questions are well worth asking, especially because Cemuhi and Paici are surrounded by toneless languages, a situation which is very unusual. [...] POC *q- developed into k- in languages to the north of the Cemuhi area, in the languages from the Hienghene area (Pije, Fwäi, Nemi, Jawe), Pwaamei and Pwapwä.
tone_statements.locator: p. 498 (sec. 1, with Map 1 'Tonal and non-tonal language areas of New Caledonia', 9 = PIJE) and p. 500 (sec. 2.2)

sources.citation: Rivierre, Jean-Claude. 1978. Accents, tons et inversion tonale en Nouvelle-Calédonie. BSLP 73(1): 415-443.
sources.note: Describes initial demarcative accent in Xârâcùù (south) and tone in the centre; the northern (Hienghène) group appears only in the consonant-series table p. 429 (examples in Jawe). No statement about Pije or Hienghène-group accent placement.

sources.note: Cèmuhî (three level tones: high, mid, low) and Paicî are the only tonal languages of the area and are 'surrounded by toneless languages'; the languages to the north, explicitly including the Hienghène languages (Pije, Fwâi, Nemi, Jawe), are non-tonal and keep aspirates/fricatives (< *CC) where Cèmuhî/Paicî developed high tone (papa > ppa > pha, fa north / pá centre); loans from these northern languages into Cèmuhî receive high tone when the donor form has an aspirated or fricative initial (Pije examples p. 501). Map 1 'Tonal and non-tonal language areas of New Caledonia' p. 498.

tone.quote: Les traits suivants sont caractéristiques des langues EN et N: - opposition entre consonnes aspirées et non-aspirées : p différent de ph, m différent de hm. [...] [2. Langues du centre et du sud (CS, S, ES)] - elles ont nettement moins de consonnes que les langues du nord et n'opposent jamais des aspirées et des non-aspirées. Dans certains groupes, le ton du mot, c'est-à-dire sa musicalité haute ou basse, supplée l'absence de distinction p/ph, m/hm etc... [...] Ce trait de musicalité (exceptionnel dans la famille linguistique austronésienne) est propre au cèmuhî, au paicî, et aux langues ES.
tone.locator: Notice of planche 19, section B 'Particularités linguistiques', 1 'Langues du nord (groupe EN et N)' and 2 'Langues du centre et du sud (CS, S, ES)' (notice unpaginated); pijé placed in groupe N in section A.2 'Nord (N)'
tone.translation: The following features are characteristic of the EN and N languages: an opposition between aspirated and non-aspirated consonants: p distinct from ph, m distinct from hm. [...] [Centre and south languages] have markedly fewer consonants than the northern languages and never oppose aspirated to non-aspirated ones. In some groups, word tone, i.e. its high or low pitch, makes up for the absence of the p/ph, m/hm distinction. [...] This pitch feature (exceptional in the Austronesian family) is specific to Cèmuhî, Paicî and the far-south (ES) languages.
tone.n_tones: None: not a tone language (word tone restricted to cèmuhî, paicî and the far-so…

sources.note: Origin of the Cèmuhî/Paicî tone systems (high tone < geminate/reduplicated onsets, corresponding to aspirated consonants in the non-tonal northern languages such as the Hienghène group; low tone < medial geminates), i.e. treats Pije and its sisters as toneless comparanda; cited as the fuller version of the summary given in Rivierre 1994 sec. 2.1 ('see Haudricourt 1968 and Rivierre 1972; a slightly different explanation is proposed in Rivierre [forthcoming]').

tone.says: Origin of the Cèmuhî/Paicî tone systems (high tone < geminate/reduplicated onsets, corresponding to aspirated consonants in the non-tonal northern languages such as the Hienghène group; low tone < medial geminates), i.e. treats Pije and its sisters as toneless comparanda; cited as the fuller version of the summary given in Rivierre 1994 sec. 2.1 ('see Haudricourt 1968 and Rivierre 1972; a slightly different explanation is proposed in Rivierre [forthcoming]').
